item.problem: The Observe phase says the strips are unlikely to snap or deform within 200 g and instructs groups to record that no fracture occurred. The summary claims that learners observed Strip B fracturing at a lower load than Strip A.
item.quote_a: Rubber strips are unlikely to snap or stay stretched within 200 g; if neither happens, groups record 'no permanent deformation or fracture up to 200 g'
item.quote_b: They observed that Strip B (fatigued/old rope) reached permanent deformation and fracture at a lower load than Strip A

items.recommendation: Rewrite the summary's observed text to match the Observe phase, where no fracture is expected in class data and fracture is shown only by teacher demo or data card.
items.reason: The summary asserts a fracture observation that the Observe phase says learners will probably not make, so it contradicts the procedure.
items.reference: Rubber strips under 200 g typically remain elastic (standard elastic-limit behaviour); fracture claims must match the recorded data.
